name: code-lru-cache
prompt: Write a Python class LRUCache with a capacity set in the constructor, a get(key) method that returns the stored value or None when the key is absent, and a put(key, value) method that inserts or updates and evicts the least-recently-used entry when over capacity. Both get and put count as use. Reply with a single complete Python code block using only the standard library, defining the class exactly as named.
code_test:
c = LRUCache(2)
c.put(1, "a")
c.put(2, "b")
assert c.get(1) == "a"
c.put(3, "c")
assert c.get(2) is None
assert c.get(1) == "a"
assert c.get(3) == "c"
c.put(4, "d")
assert c.get(1) is None or c.get(3) is None
print("ok")

name: code-merge-intervals
prompt: Write a Python function merge_intervals(intervals) that takes a list of [start, end] pairs (ints, possibly unsorted, possibly touching) and returns the merged list sorted by start, treating touching intervals like [1,4] and [4,5] as one. Reply with a single complete Python code block using only the standard library, defining the function exactly as named.
code_test:
assert merge_intervals([[1, 3], [2, 6], [8, 10], [15, 18]]) == [[1, 6], [8, 10], [15, 18]]
assert merge_intervals([]) == []
assert merge_intervals([[1, 4], [4, 5]]) == [[1, 5]]
assert merge_intervals([[5, 6], [1, 2]]) == [[1, 2], [5, 6]]
print("ok")

name: code-rle
prompt: Write a Python function rle(s) that run-length-encodes a string: 'aaabcc' becomes 'a3b1c2'. The empty string returns ''. Reply with a single complete Python code block using only the standard library, defining the function exactly as named.
code_test:
assert rle("aaabcc") == "a3b1c2"
assert rle("") == ""
assert rle("a") == "a1"
assert rle("abba") == "a1b2a1"
print("ok")

name: code-debug-mutable-default
prompt:
Users report that tags from different items leak into each other when using this Python helper. Explain why in one short paragraph, then give a fixed version in a single complete Python code block (keep the name add_tag and the same call shape):

def add_tag(tag, tags=[]):
    tags.append(tag)
    return tags
code_test:
a = add_tag("x")
b = add_tag("y")
assert b == ["y"], b
assert a == ["x"], a
assert add_tag("z", ["q"]) == ["q", "z"]
print("ok")

name: code-csv-top-spenders
prompt: Write a Python function top_spenders(csv_text, n) that takes CSV text with header 'name,amount' (amount is a number, names repeat) and returns a list of the n names with the highest total amount, highest first. Reply with a single complete Python code block using only the standard library, defining the function exactly as named.
code_test:
text = "name,amount
ann,10
bob,5
ann,3
cid,9
bob,2
"
assert top_spenders(text, 2) == ["ann", "cid"]
assert top_spenders(text, 1) == ["ann"]
assert top_spenders("name,amount
", 3) == []
print("ok")

name: code-roman-numerals
prompt: Write a Python function int_to_roman(n) that converts an integer from 1 to 3999 into a Roman numeral string. Reply with a single complete Python code block using only the standard library, defining the function exactly as named.
code_test:
assert int_to_roman(1994) == "MCMXCIV"
assert int_to_roman(4) == "IV"
assert int_to_roman(9) == "IX"
assert int_to_roman(3999) == "MMMCMXCIX"
assert int_to_roman(1) == "I"
print("ok")
